The previous chapters describe a broad theory of machine hearing: physical observation, musical structure, trustworthy process, internal representation, judgment, uncertainty, evidence, reporting, Production Cases, learning and controlled intervention.
It is defined by whether one narrow hearing loop can run reproducibly from source registration to evidence-backed judgment and validated case closure.

It says that, within a bounded set of judgment families, Moodify can hear reproducibly enough to produce structured representation, calibrated judgment, evidence, uncertainty and a reusable Production Case.
Report generation is a projection of that case, and learning remains gated after review.
Any execution path that bypasses source identity, representation, judgment evidence or case closure is not canonical Ear v1 behavior.

Work is in scope only when it materially improves one of five capabilities: | Capability | Phase I question | | --- | --- | | Listen | Can the system observe the source reliably? | | Represent | Can observations become a stable auditory state? | | Judge | Can bounded semantic conclusions be made with references? | | Explain / Evidence | Can claims be reconstructed and inspected? | | Learn | Can reviewed cases create validated future improvement? | Features that are attractive but do not improve these five capabilities should not block v1.
The engineering question for every proposed task is simple: *does this make the Ear hear, represent, judge, explain or learn more reliably?* If not, it is deferred.
The Intervention Lab may contain transformations resembling mastering or audio effects, but those transformations exist to test hearing.
Each family must have a semantic definition, evidence contract, reference policy, uncertainty policy and benchmark.
The family also declares which conditions force UNCERTAIN or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
The sensor pack should be versioned as one production unit so that benchmark runs remain comparable.

Not every useful sensor belongs in the canonical completion path. | Tier | Capability | v1 status | | --- | --- | --- | | B | CQT / long-window low-frequency detail | conditional | | B | frequency-dependent phase analysis | conditional | | B | learned artifact embedding | conditional | | B | source-separated stem measurements | conditional; separator provenance required | | R | new experimental descriptors | research only | | R | heavy foundation-model representations | research unless benchmark gain is proven | Tier B capabilities may run when a judgment family requires them or when resource policy allows.
Research sensors can generate experimental evidence without affecting case completion.
The schema must preserve typed values, time support, status, confidence and provenance.
If used, their model, checkpoint, pooling and time support must be recorded.

Ear v1 must treat missingness as semantic information. | Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | PRESENT | valid field/evidence exists | | NOT_RUN | capability intentionally not executed | | FAILED | attempted capability failed | | NOT_APPLICABLE | capability does not apply | | INSUFFICIENT_CONFIDENCE | estimate exists but is not reliable enough for use | | DEGRADED | usable partial result under declared degraded policy | Zero is a value.
INSUFFICIENT_CONFIDENCE is an epistemic state.
This status vocabulary should be common across sensors, representation fields and evidence contracts.
All mechanisms emit the same JudgmentRecord contract.
Confidence is empirical support for the finding.
A high-severity, low-confidence finding can be a review candidate without being reported as fact.

Every judgment family requires an explicit abstention policy. | Condition | Semantic outcome | | --- | --- | | required evidence missing | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | | evidence complete but support below threshold | UNCERTAIN | | high novelty/OOD | confidence reduction + cautious language | | strong model/sensor disagreement | surface conflict; consider review | | unusual evidence without validated class | UNKNOWN_ANOMALY_CANDIDATE | | support above calibrated family policy | SUPPORTED judgment | The acceptance threshold should be calibrated per family rather than globally.
Causal or novel artifact labels require stricter support than direct physical findings.
Unknown anomaly is a valid research outcome when unusual evidence exists but no validated family explains it.
Every authoritative judgment must resolve to evidence.
Evidence should identify the source interval, relevant representation fields, reference basis, producer versions and any rendered artifact used for inspection.
A model score alone is insufficient evidence for high-authority physical judgments when the underlying signal evidence is available.
If mandatory evidence cannot be resolved, the finding cannot enter SUPPORTED status.

It requires grounded explanation for the first judgment families. | Requirement | Ear v1 minimum | | --- | --- | | grounding | explanation only from JudgmentRecord + EvidenceGraph | | time localization | seconds; musical coordinates when reliable | | direct physical paths | measurement/reference -> judgment | | causal discipline | association vs causal hypothesis separated | | evidence bundle | per authoritative finding | | learned XAI | experimental unless faithfulness benchmark passes | Direct physical judgments should be explainable by construction.
Learned artifact hypotheses may use post-hoc methods experimentally, but their language should remain conservative until faithfulness is validated.
The report generator is never allowed to add causal claims absent from the JudgmentRecord.

The primary user-facing artifact is the Auditory Report. | Report component | v1 minimum | | --- | --- | | identity/status | SourceID, CaseID, Ear version, analysis status | | summary | key supported + unresolved findings | | finding cards | class, location, severity, confidence, reference, reason | | evidence | resolvable key artifacts/measurements | | uncertainty | UNCERTAIN / INSUFFICIENT / UNKNOWN section | | coverage | what ran / failed / was not applicable | | provenance appendix | run/config/sensor/model/report versions | | machine JSON | canonical report record | The report should avoid a global quality score.
It should answer what was heard, where, why it matters, how certain the Ear is, what evidence supports it and what remains unknown.

A canonical Ear v1 run is not complete until the Production Case contains a minimum durable record. | Case component | Required | | --- | --- | | CaseID / SourceID / RunID | yes | | objective/specification | yes | | state/event history | yes | | run/version manifest | yes | | MeasurementRecord | yes | | AuditoryRepresentation v1 | yes | | JudgmentRecords | yes | | Evidence index | yes for authoritative findings | | machine/human report | yes | | HumanReview support | yes as interface; review may be pending | | LearningRecord support | yes | | closure manifest | yes | The case is the unit of learning, regression and institutional memory.
A report without a closed case is a transient output rather than a validated hearing event.

Ear v1 needs a compact review interface because learning depends on error decomposition. | Review outcome | Required use | | --- | --- | | accepted | confirm supported judgment | | rejected | semantic error | | false positive / false negative | benchmark/learning signal | | severity adjusted | policy learning | | confidence adjusted | calibration learning | | context/evidence corrected | MSE/evidence learning | | new phenomenon | research/ontology candidate | | insufficient evidence confirmed | coverage/sensor learning | Review should target the exact JudgmentID and evidence.
A reviewed case becomes eligible for LearningRecord generation when the required review fields are complete.

requirements.section: 21. Learning in v1 Is Offline and Gated
requirements.requirement_text: Reviewed cases create LearningRecords and candidate changes.

requirements.section: 21. Learning in v1 Is Offline and Gated
requirements.requirement_text: Candidate versions are tested separately and promoted only after regression and benchmark validation.

requirements.section: 21. Learning in v1 Is Offline and Gated
requirements.requirement_text: This preserves historical behavior and prevents one anomalous review from mutating global judgment policy.
Intervention results contribute benchmark and LearningRecords.

Ear v1 should expose a small number of stable interfaces rather than many user features. | Interface | Purpose | | --- | --- | | CLI | reproducible case lifecycle and regression | | Case API/service | canonical programmatic operations | | App report view | human review and inspection | | machine report JSON | interoperability / future clients | | artifact store | evidence and large arrays | | research namespace | Intervention Lab / experimental sensors separated from production | The CLI is especially valuable for deterministic regression and research automation.
Resource discipline makes the benchmark reproducible, keeps cloud cost bounded and forces the system to justify expensive models by measurable judgment gains.
A candidate model that improves one benchmark point while multiplying cost by twenty should not be adopted automatically.
The engineering objective is trustworthy evidence per unit of compute.

Different outputs require different reproducibility contracts. | Class | Ear v1 use | | --- | --- | | bitwise | hashes, canonical serialization, selected deterministic records | | tolerance | FFT/resampling/numeric measurements | | semantic | judgment/evidence relation remains unchanged | | statistical | only for explicitly stochastic research/learned components | Canonical WSE measurements should aim for bitwise or tolerance determinism.
Learned embeddings may use semantic or statistical reproducibility depending on backend.
The case manifest records the declared class for important outputs so that replay differences can be interpreted correctly.
Every case must preserve enough identity to reproduce its execution context.
Mutable filenames, current working directory or runtime defaults are not sufficient provenance.

A first benchmark should contain several complementary case families. | Case family | Purpose | | --- | --- | | clean/reference tracks | baseline false-positive behavior | | controlled Intervention Cases | known physical effects | | hard negatives | intentional production choices resembling anomalies | | AI-generated production cases | target domain | | unknown/new generator cases | OOD/novelty behavior | | failure/input-integrity cases | PPE and refusal semantics | | Golden Cases | detailed regression | | human-reviewed ambiguous cases | abstention/calibration boundary | The benchmark must contain both positive and negative examples.
Benchmark versioning is required so that performance across Ear releases remains comparable.

No single metric should define Ear v1. | Dimension | Examples | | --- | --- | | detection | sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall | | calibration | reliability/ECE/Brier where appropriate | | selective prediction | coverage + selective risk | | localization | time/frequency support error | | evidence | completeness + resolvability | | reproducibility | bitwise/tolerance match | | report | regeneration + cross-view semantic fidelity | | learning | reviewed case -> LearningRecord -> candidate traceability | | resource | latency, memory, compute, storage | Direct detectors may emphasize sensitivity/specificity.
Explainability requires evidence completeness and localization.
PPE requires reproducibility and report regeneration.
The benchmark should surface tradeoffs rather than hide them inside one composite score.
Golden Cases protect known detailed behavior: source identity, core measurements, judgment semantics, evidence resolution and package integrity.
Unexpected changes in a Golden Case block release until the difference is reviewed or deliberately re-baselined.
Failure-injection tests are particularly important because missing evidence and invalid state transitions must remain visible.

A reliable system must also prove that it refuses invalid completion. | Negative case | Expected behavior | | --- | --- | | corrupt input | reject before semantic analysis | | required sensor failure | block affected authoritative judgment | | missing evidence artifact | case cannot close as fully evidenced | | low-confidence MSE | disable/soften dependent contextual judgment | | OOD high | reduce authority; do not invent defect | | invalid state transition | reject transition | | attempt to mutate closed case | append new record/fork; no silent rewrite | | post-processing unavailable | canonical Ear still completes | The system passes these tests when it blocks semantic overreach.
A case that correctly stops at INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is a successful test of the Ear.
Ear v1 should collect the technical metadata required for reproducibility without expanding into rights-management logic.
The Ear records technical identity but does not infer ownership from audio.
Secrets such as API tokens are never stored in Production Case evidence.
This keeps asset provenance and legal rights distinct.

Production operation needs a narrow observability layer. | Operational signal | Use | | --- | --- | | case state counts | throughput / stuck cases | | failure class counts | runtime reliability | | latency/memory | resource budget | | optional model availability | degraded-capability monitoring | | evidence-packaging failures | PPE integrity | | report regeneration failures | case durability | | benchmark drift alerts | release/recalibration research trigger | Metrics should describe case throughput and failures without replacing case-level evidence.
Operational logs may be transient, but failure-relevant logs referenced by a closed failed case should be retained according to policy.

requirements.requirement_text: The purpose of freeze is to convert a broad research program into a testable artifact.

requirements.section: 41. What Counts as Evidence That Ear v1 Exists?
requirements.requirement_text: It is a set of reproducible cases showing that the system detects known physical phenomena, avoids known false positives, preserves uncertainty, reconstructs evidence and learns from review.

requirements.section: 41. What Counts as Evidence That Ear v1 Exists?
requirements.requirement_text: The claim becomes progressively stronger as the number and diversity of validated cases increase.

requirements.section: 41. What Counts as Evidence That Ear v1 Exists?
requirements.requirement_text: Ear v1 exists when the architecture is no longer only a diagram: its contracts are executable, its mistakes are measurable and its outputs survive the run that produced them.

It is closure: the system can register a source, observe it, represent it, judge a bounded set of phenomena, preserve uncertainty, expose evidence, create a report, close a Production Case, accept human review and generate a controlled learning candidate.
The Judgment Engine is hybrid, evidence-constrained and uncertainty-aware.** **7.
The Auditory Report is the primary user-facing artifact.** **8.
CPU-first execution keeps the first claim reproducible and economical.** **10.
Benchmarks, Golden Cases and failure tests define readiness.** **11.
Intervention validates hearing but never becomes required processing.** **12.
Ear v1 exists only when the full closed loop is demonstrably reproducible.**

Moodify Ear v1 is intentionally small: a stable physical sensor pack, minimal musical context, a versioned Auditory Representation, eight bounded judgment families, calibrated uncertainty, evidence-backed explanations, a canonical Auditory Report, Production Cases, Human Review and an offline learning interface.
The engineering task for August 2026 is therefore precise: build the first closed, reproducible and falsifiable Ear.

requirements.section: 1. A Benchmark Should Reveal the Boundary of Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: It is an instrument for discovering where a system works, where it fails, and how confidently those boundaries are known.

requirements.section: 1. A Benchmark Should Reveal the Boundary of Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: Ear v1 therefore needs a benchmark that exposes capability by judgment family, evidence type, context, uncertainty state and domain slice.

requirements.section: 1. A Benchmark Should Reveal the Boundary of Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: The governing principle is: *a benchmark should reveal the boundary of hearing, not hide it.*
Moodify's benchmark does not measure one model.
It measures the behavior of the complete hearing system.
The evaluated object includes decoding, sensors, Auditory Representation, structural context, Judgment Engine, uncertainty policy, evidence generation and Production Case closure.
This distinction is important because a high-performing classifier can still belong to an unreliable Ear if evidence cannot be reconstructed or the case cannot be replayed.
The benchmark therefore combines capability metrics with trust metrics.

Every benchmark item should help answer at least one explicit scientific question. | Question | Example evidence | | --- | --- | | Can it detect? | positive controls, natural positives | | Can it avoid false alarms? | negative controls, hard negatives | | Can it localize? | known intervention windows / reviewed intervals | | Can it know uncertainty? | ambiguous, low-evidence, OOD cases | | Can it explain? | evidence completeness / faithfulness | | Can it reproduce? | replay, Golden Cases, report regeneration | | Can it generalize? | generator/time/domain slices | | Can it learn? | benchmark delta after validated promotion | The corpus should not grow by collecting audio indiscriminately.
Each case enters because it tests a known dimension of hearing.
This keeps the benchmark interpretable and prevents size from becoming a substitute for coverage.

requirements.section: 4. The Benchmark Is a Versioned Asset
requirements.requirement_text: If the dataset, labels, reference policy or metric implementation changes, the benchmark version changes.

requirements.section: 4. The Benchmark Is a Versioned Asset
requirements.requirement_text: Ear v2 can be evaluated on the Ear v1 core benchmark even if a later suite adds new generator families or judgment classes.

requirements.section: 4. The Benchmark Is a Versioned Asset
requirements.requirement_text: A benchmark update should document what was added, removed, corrected or relabeled.

requirements.section: 4. The Benchmark Is a Versioned Asset
requirements.requirement_text: Historical scores remain attached to the benchmark version that produced them.

Ear v1 should use a layered corpus rather than one undifferentiated test set. | Layer | Purpose | | --- | --- | | Controlled Intervention | known physical cause and strength | | Natural Reviewed | real production complexity | | Hard Negative | semantic restraint / artistic extremes | | Golden Cases | fine-grained regression memory | | OOD / Unknown | novelty and uncertainty behavior | | Failure / Integrity | input/PPE refusal behavior | | Calibration | threshold and confidence fitting | | Protected Release Test | final unbiased release estimate | The layers serve different purposes.
Positive controls establish sensitivity and localization behavior without requiring subjective labeling.
Natural clean cases also provide negatives, but their “clean” status should be reviewed rather than assumed.
This tests whether the Ear responds to incidental pipeline artifacts rather than the intended manipulation.
If the detector changes only because a file passed through a tool, the benchmark has exposed a shortcut.

Hard negatives are examples that resemble the target phenomenon but should not receive the target judgment. | Target family | Hard negative example | | --- | --- | | HF cutoff | intentional lo-fi / telephone-style artistic filter | | LF accumulation | bass-heavy genre with stable intentional low end | | stereo imbalance | purposefully asymmetric intro/effect | | phase risk | wide decorrelation that remains mono-safe | | compression anomaly | intentional dense loud master | | transient irregularity | soft-attack arrangement / legato texture | | AI artifact hypothesis | human-produced sound with similar spectral signature | Hard negatives define the semantic boundary of the Ear.
They reveal whether the system can distinguish an acoustic characteristic from a technical defect or artifact.
For Moodify, this is one of the most important benchmark categories because artistic production deliberately creates many extreme acoustic states.
A natural positive case is a real audio example in which reviewers agree that a narrowly defined judgment family is present and the required evidence is available.
They should therefore validate the judgment semantics, not necessarily a causal story.
Aggregate performance can hide domain-specific failure.

The benchmark should preserve slices for known source domains. | Slice | Why preserve it | | --- | --- | | generator family | model-specific artifacts/drift | | unknown generator | open-world behavior | | time cohort | ecosystem evolution | | genre/texture | different acoustic baselines | | vocal vs instrumental | different structural/evidence regimes | | sample rate / codec | format-dependent measurement conditions | | short vs long track | different temporal coverage | | simple vs complex arrangement | sensor/MSE difficulty | Generator identity may be unavailable for some cases; those should remain in an UNKNOWN domain rather than being guessed.
Slice metrics reveal drift before it becomes invisible inside a global average.
An Intervention derivative should normally remain in the same split family as its parent unless the benchmark is explicitly designed otherwise.
Alternate encodes, previews or stems from the same work can also create leakage.

requirements.section: 13. Calibration Set and Test Set Are Different
requirements.requirement_text: Thresholds and confidence calibration must be chosen without using the final test set.

requirements.section: 13. Calibration Set and Test Set Are Different
requirements.requirement_text: The test set estimates the resulting behavior.

requirements.section: 13. Calibration Set and Test Set Are Different
requirements.requirement_text: If the same cases are repeatedly used to tune decisions, the benchmark gradually becomes a training set.

requirements.section: 14. Benchmark Slices Must Be Declared Before Looking at Results
requirements.requirement_text: Core release slices should be declared in the benchmark contract.

requirements.section: 14. Benchmark Slices Must Be Declared Before Looking at Results
requirements.requirement_text: Unexpected post-hoc failure clusters can still be reported, but should be labeled exploratory and may become official slices in the next benchmark version.
Moodify should often prioritize precision for semantically aggressive labels such as likely AI artifact, while direct physical risk detectors may tolerate a different tradeoff.
F1 can summarize precision and recall, but should never replace the two component metrics.
Specificity measures how often negative cases remain negative.
Confidence quality is benchmarked separately from classification quality.
Reliability diagrams, Expected Calibration Error, Brier score and log loss provide complementary views of whether confidence reflects empirical correctness [3-5].
Calibration must be measured per judgment family and, where sample size permits, per important domain slice.
Because Ear v1 can abstain, evaluation must measure how much of the domain it chooses to judge.

Abstention should be scored as a semantic outcome. | Outcome | Benchmark interpretation | | --- | --- | | correct accepted | successful hearing | | incorrect accepted | overreach/error | | appropriate UNCERTAIN | successful restraint | | appropriate INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | successful evidence discipline | | unnecessary abstention | lost coverage | | forced unsupported judgment | semantic failure | The benchmark should include cases intentionally designed to be ambiguous or evidence-limited.
These cases test whether the Ear can avoid forced conclusions.
A correct UNCERTAIN or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE result can therefore count as success.
The benchmark must contain cases outside the known validation distribution.
OpenOOD and related benchmark work emphasize that OOD evaluation is highly sensitive to how in-distribution and out-of-distribution data are defined [7,8].
It is to reduce unjustified semantic certainty when the case lies outside validated support.
Localization can be measured using interval overlap, onset/offset error or tolerance-window hit rate depending on the phenomenon.
Severity is a policy judgment and should not be benchmarked as if it were a direct physical measurement.
Where severity labels are used, the benchmark should define the consequence scale and reviewer protocol.
If reviewers disagree substantially, the family may require narrower definitions or confidence intervals rather than a single ground-truth severity.
A judgment is not production-ready if its required evidence cannot be reconstructed.
Evidence completeness should be benchmarked independently of judgment correctness.
A detector can be accurate but fail the release gate if its authoritative findings lack required measurements, time support, reference or provenance.
This is how Moodify ensures that benchmark optimization does not bypass explainability.
For learned judgments that use post-hoc explanations, benchmark evaluation should test whether the cited evidence actually influences the decision.
Perturbation-based tests can remove or alter the regions identified as important and measure the judgment response.
Audio explanation research has shown that explanation behavior depends strongly on the perturbation design, so the explanation benchmark itself must be specified carefully [9-11].
Direct rule-based physical findings usually have simpler faithfulness paths because the evidence is intrinsic to the decision.

Benchmarking hearing also means benchmarking whether the same case can be reproduced. | Reproducibility layer | Metric / contract | | --- | --- | | source identity | hash equality | | canonical serialization | bitwise equality | | numeric sensors | absolute/relative tolerance | | judgment semantics | class/reference/evidence relation stability | | learned stochastic component | declared statistical tolerance | | report | semantic field equality across regeneration | | case package | manifest/artifact integrity | A release benchmark should include replay on the reference environment and, where practical, on a second supported environment.
Every benchmark case should be able to regenerate its Auditory Report from the closed Production Case.
This tests that report content is truly derived from canonical case artifacts rather than hidden runtime state.
Cross-view semantic consistency can also be tested: PDF, app and machine JSON should show the same judgment IDs, severity, confidence and evidence relationships.
The Ear is evaluated on detection, localization, confidence response, monotonicity, evidence and false triggers in controls.
This benchmark does not prove artistic understanding.
If intervention strength alpha increases, the relevant evidence should generally respond in a predictable direction.
The threshold should be expressed with confidence intervals and under a declared source population, because detectability depends on musical context.
This turns vague claims such as “Moodify can hear subtle phase problems” into measurable statements.
Invariance tests are a defense against shortcut learning.
If a bandwidth detector changes when the filename changes, the benchmark has exposed non-auditory behavior.
Counterfactual benchmark cases ask whether changing the evidence that should matter changes the judgment.
For phase risk, the benchmark can alter inter-channel delay while holding other properties approximately constant.
A counterfactual benchmark complements ordinary accuracy by testing directional dependence.
They are deliberately small and carefully reviewed.
A Golden Case can assert expected sensor fields, tolerance ranges, judgment semantics, evidence references and report integrity.
Unexpected changes block release until explained.
Ear v1 should report uncertainty around benchmark metrics.
Bootstrap intervals are a practical nonparametric approach for many metrics, provided resampling respects the appropriate independent unit [12].

requirements.section: 35. Statistical Significance Is Not Practical Significance
requirements.requirement_text: Release decisions should therefore consider effect size, confidence interval, affected judgment families, resource cost and regression risk.

requirements.section: 35. Statistical Significance Is Not Practical Significance
requirements.requirement_text: The benchmark is an engineering decision tool, not a contest to maximize p-values.
As the number of metrics and slices grows, some apparent improvements will occur by chance.
Core release metrics and gates should be predeclared.
Benchmark mining is particularly dangerous when teams repeatedly tune against the same test corpus.
Protected holdouts and benchmark refreshes help preserve validity.
Natural benchmark labels depend on human review.

The benchmark should therefore measure label quality. | Quality field | Benchmark use | | --- | --- | | reviewer role | authority/provenance | | agreement | label ambiguity | | review confidence | weak vs strong ground truth | | evidence inspected | review completeness | | disagreement notes | uncertainty slice | | correction history | benchmark-version lineage | Inter-rater disagreement can indicate ambiguous cases or poorly defined judgment families.
Such cases may belong in an uncertainty benchmark instead of a hard-labeled test set.
The benchmark should preserve reviewer provenance and correction history rather than hiding disagreements.
Each benchmark release should include a data card or dataset documentation describing composition, collection, labels, exclusions, known biases, intended use and rights constraints.
Datasheets for Datasets and related documentation frameworks emphasize that evaluation data needs explicit context because benchmark results inherit the limitations of the corpus [13,14].
Moodify should additionally document source lineage and whether a case is natural, controlled, derivative, synthetic or human-reviewed.
A benchmark without documentation can create precise numbers with unclear meaning.
Benchmark reproducibility does not imply that all audio can be redistributed publicly.
The benchmark manifest should separate technical identity from access policy.
Internal cases may be reproducible within Moodify while public releases use redistributable or derived evidence.
Governance should preserve scientific traceability without violating source restrictions.
If a test case or near-duplicate appears in the validated retrieval corpus, the Ear may seem to generalize while simply remembering the answer.
Benchmark evaluation should freeze the allowed retrieval corpus and exclude test-lineage cases.
The report should record retrieval-corpus version so that the benchmark can be reproduced.
External memory is part of the Ear and must therefore be benchmarked like a model parameter.

requirements.section: 41. Benchmark Leakage Through Repeated Human Tuning
requirements.requirement_text: Even without formal training, repeated inspection of test failures can cause the development team to overfit engineering decisions to the benchmark.

requirements.section: 41. Benchmark Leakage Through Repeated Human Tuning
requirements.requirement_text: Moodify should maintain an internal development benchmark and a more protected release benchmark.

requirements.section: 41. Benchmark Leakage Through Repeated Human Tuning
requirements.requirement_text: When the release benchmark becomes too familiar, a new protected version should be introduced while retaining the old suite for historical comparison.

requirements.section: 41. Benchmark Leakage Through Repeated Human Tuning
requirements.requirement_text: The objective is to preserve the benchmark's ability to surprise the team.

A release dashboard should present a matrix of capability rather than a global score. | Row / column | Suggested content | | --- | --- | | Rows | 8 judgment families + uncertainty/OOD + case integrity | | Detection | precision / recall / specificity | | Confidence | ECE/Brier/reliability | | Selective | coverage / selective risk | | Localization | IoU / timing error | | Evidence | completeness / faithfulness | | Reproducibility | replay/report regeneration | | Slices | generator/time/hard-negative/OOD deltas | The dashboard can show judgment families as rows and dimensions such as precision, recall, calibration, coverage, localization, evidence completeness and reproducibility as columns.
Domain slices can then reveal which generator or case families account for failures.
A family that fails its gate remains disabled or research-only.
Ear v1 can ship with fewer authoritative families if evidence does not support all eight.
A benchmark is valuable when it discovers that the Ear is weaker than expected.
A failed release gate identifies where more research is needed.
The team should preserve failure cases as Production Cases and convert important patterns into LearningRecords.
Benchmarking is therefore part of the learning loop, not merely a final exam.
A benchmark that never threatens the release is probably not testing enough.

requirements.section: 45. Benchmarking the Growth of the Ear
requirements.requirement_text: Ear v3 may improve artifact intelligence but should continue to pass protected physical Golden Cases.

requirements.section: 45. Benchmarking the Growth of the Ear
requirements.requirement_text: Longitudinal benchmarking makes the evolution of auditory intelligence visible rather than anecdotal.
Benchmarking Hearing can be summarized by twelve principles. **1.
Benchmark the complete Ear, not only a model.** **2.
Correct abstention is a benchmarkable success.** **6.
Localization and evidence completeness matter as much as class accuracy.** **7.
Intervention cases measure mechanistic sensitivity.** **8.
Invariance and counterfactual tests defend against shortcuts.** **9.
Confidence intervals expose uncertainty in the benchmark itself.** **10.
Benchmark failures become LearningRecords and future research.**

It requires a benchmark that tests what the Ear detects, what it misses, when it abstains, where it localizes evidence, how confidence behaves, whether explanations resolve, and whether the same case can be reproduced.
The benchmark must contain easy positives, hard negatives, controlled interventions, natural cases, new domains and explicit unknowns.
It must measure both capability and restraint.
Most importantly, the benchmark should resist the temptation to compress hearing into one flattering number.

requirements.section: 1. A Version Is a Capability State
requirements.requirement_text: It should represent a coherent capability state: what the machine can hear, under which conditions, with what evidence, and with what measured limits.

requirements.section: 1. A Version Is a Capability State
requirements.requirement_text: The governing principle is: *every new Ear must add a new form of hearing while preserving the validated hearing of the previous Ear.*
Promotion to a new Ear generation depends on evidence, benchmarks and stable Production Cases.
The roadmap therefore prioritizes changes that expand perception, context, judgment, uncertainty, evidence or learning.
The inheritance set contains Golden Cases, benchmark slices, judgment-family contracts and evidence requirements that must continue to pass unless a deliberate semantic revision is declared.
A new Ear is not allowed to improve contextual intelligence by forgetting stable clipping detection or phase evidence.

requirements.section: 6. What v1 Must Leave Behind as Assets
requirements.requirement_text: A successful v1 release produces more than code. | Asset | Why it matters later | | --- | --- | | validated Production Cases | training, retrieval, research memory | | Golden Cases | protected regression core | | Intervention cases | causal physical benchmark | | error corpus | historical false positives/negatives/overconfidence | | Representation v1 | stable shared internal language | | judgment contracts | semantic lineage | | benchmark v1 | baseline for every future Ear | These assets are the seed crystal for later versions.

requirements.section: 6. What v1 Must Leave Behind as Assets
requirements.requirement_text: It begins from a corpus of known physical hearing events, reviewed errors, benchmark controls and versioned representations.
The transition requires contextual hearing to measurably improve judgment.
Examples include reduced false positives through section context, better internal references from repetition, or more accurate interpretation of dynamic/spectral changes by musical role.
The v1 protected physical benchmark must remain within regression limits.

The benchmark must evolve with the new capability. | Benchmark | v2 question | | --- | --- | | context reversal | does correct structure change the judgment? | | repetition hard negatives | are repeated intentional changes protected? | | boundary uncertainty | does uncertain MSE reduce downstream confidence? | | section transfer | does context generalize across forms/genres? | | v1 regression | are physical capabilities preserved? | Ear v2 should be rewarded when structural context prevents a false positive, not merely when a section label is correct.

Context can create new errors. | Failure | Risk | | --- | --- | | wrong beat grid | mislocalized structure | | wrong section boundary | false expectedness/anomaly | | overconfident structure | downstream false certainty | | genre-specific form assumptions | poor transfer | | source-role leakage | wrong contextual explanation | A wrong section boundary can suppress a real anomaly.
Ear v2 therefore needs uncertainty propagation from structural estimates into judgment confidence.
More context should increase intelligence, not hide uncertainty.
The transition to Ear v3 begins when the system can recognize recurring artifact phenomena across AI-generated music beyond simple physical thresholds.

The system should demonstrate that learned and case-based representations identify patterns that reviewed experts recognize as recurring generation-related phenomena, while maintaining causal discipline.
The benchmark must include human-produced hard negatives and new generator families to prevent the Ear from learning shortcuts such as codec, metadata or genre.
The system may recognize an artifact pattern without claiming to identify the exact model or causal mechanism.
Ear v3 needs an artifact ontology, but ontology should follow evidence.
A candidate phenomenon should accumulate multiple cases, stable representation signatures, reviewer agreement and a benchmark before becoming a production Judgment Family.
Ear v3 may introduce dedicated learned representation spaces for artifact similarity.
Moodify can fine-tune or adapt representations for artifact retrieval, but the embedding is only one layer.
WSE evidence and contextual structure remain necessary for explanation and false-positive control.

Some artifact patterns may be associated with one generator family, while others may recur across many systems. | Knowledge type | Example | Durability | | --- | --- | --- | | generator-specific | pattern strongly tied to one known model family | may drift rapidly | | workflow-specific | artifact tied to codec/export chain | moderate | | generator-agnostic | recurring acoustic failure across systems | potentially durable | | unknown | stable unusual pattern without established class | research frontier | Ear v3 should preserve this distinction.
The ontology should never infer generator identity solely from weak acoustic similarity without validation.
As artifact intelligence grows, the system must resist closing the world too early.
If every new artifact is forced into the nearest known label, the ontology stops learning.
Moodify should combine novelty evidence, uncertainty and case clustering.

requirements.section: 19. v3 Case Retrieval as External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: By Ear v3, the validated case library may become large enough to act as external memory.

requirements.section: 19. v3 Case Retrieval as External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: A new observation can be compared with reviewed artifact cases using several representation views.

requirements.section: 19. v3 Case Retrieval as External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: The retrieval system must remain versioned and benchmarked because changing the memory corpus changes the effective behavior of the Ear.
Structural representation must retain uncertainty and support multiple musical organizations.
A symbolic estimate must therefore carry model identity and uncertainty.
The system can model roles such as vocal, bass, percussion, harmonic bed, lead, texture or transient layer where evidence supports them.
These tests help distinguish acoustic abnormality from structural intention.

Structural hearing requires new benchmark layers. | Benchmark | Question | | --- | --- | | structure segmentation | are relevant boundaries/relations correct? | | repetition reasoning | can the Ear compare equivalent musical regions? | | role alignment | do source-role changes explain acoustic events? | | symbolic alignment | are score/MIDI/lyrics mapped reliably when supplied? | | downstream judgment gain | does richer structure improve hearing? | | v1-v3 regression | are prior capabilities protected? | Performance should be measured not only on transcription-like labels, but on whether structural representation improves downstream hearing and explanation.
The system should transfer learned auditory principles across broader music styles, production contexts and possibly non-musical sound while preserving uncertainty and provenance.

Ear v5 is a long-term research direction: a system that can construct reusable auditory representations, interpret context, form hypotheses, judge with uncertainty, explain evidence and learn from cases across a broad range of sound.
The term generalized does not imply perfect hearing or human equivalence.
The HEAR and MARBLE benchmarks reflect a related research ambition: evaluate audio or music representations through broad task transfer rather than one narrow classifier [19,20].
Moodify's contribution would be to combine transfer with case-based evidence, uncertainty and production trust.
Keeping axes separate prevents the word “general” from becoming an untestable marketing claim.

requirements.section: 30. Learned Front Ends and Adaptive Sensors
requirements.requirement_text: Moodify should adopt learned sensors only when they improve downstream hearing while preserving reproducibility and evidence.

Auditory Representation must evolve without breaking historical knowledge. | Generation | Representation emphasis | | --- | --- | | v1 | physical WSE + minimal MSE + provenance | | v2 | richer context graph and internal references | | v3 | artifact latent spaces + retrieval indices | | v4 | hierarchical structural/source-role relations | | v5 | transferable plural auditory state across domains | Each generation should preserve the ability to read historical cases under their original representation contract.
A family may become more context-sensitive, split into narrower subtypes, gain stronger evidence requirements or be deprecated when its semantics prove unstable.
Ear v2 may reduce uncertainty by adding structural context.
Ear v3 may increase uncertainty appropriately on unknown generator families.
Better uncertainty can look like more abstention in a newly expanded domain before new learning reduces it.

As semantic claims become more complex, evidence requirements must become stronger. | Generation | Evidence burden | | --- | --- | | v1 | direct physical measurements + simple context | | v2 | physical evidence + structural reference | | v3 | physical + learned + retrieved cases + domain uncertainty | | v4 | multi-level structural relations + counterfactual/context evidence | | v5 | cross-domain evidence with explicit transfer limits | A direct clipping judgment can be supported by simple physical evidence.
A claim about recurring AI-artifact morphology may require physical, learned, case-based and contextual evidence together.
Later Ear versions should not gain semantic authority faster than their evidence architecture.
Benchmark suites must grow in layers while preserving protected historical cores.
Later versions add contextual, artifact, structural and transfer tasks.
A benchmark version should never erase earlier failure history merely to make the new Ear look stronger.

The Production Case library should become more diverse as the Ear evolves. | Generation | Case corpus emphasis | | --- | --- | | v1 | physical positives/negatives/interventions | | v2 | context reversals/repetition/structure ambiguity | | v3 | artifact clusters/generator slices/hard negatives | | v4 | structural relations/symbolic alignments/source roles | | v5 | cross-domain transfer and open-world cases | The corpus increasingly serves three functions: benchmark memory, external retrieval memory and training/research data.

requirements.section: 38. From Batch Learning to Adaptive Learning
requirements.requirement_text: Future versions may gradually shorten the learning cycle, but adaptation should remain observable. | Mode | When appropriate | | --- | --- | | offline batch | Ear v1 default; strongest reproducibility | | frequent batch | larger reviewed corpus with mature promotion gates | | shadow adaptive | candidate updates evaluated continuously but not authoritative | | constrained online | future only with strong rollback, drift and audit controls | | silent online mutation | not acceptable as canonical Moodify behavior | A move toward faster adaptation requires stronger monitoring, shadow evaluation, rollback and data-quality controls.

requirements.section: 38. From Batch Learning to Adaptive Learning
requirements.requirement_text: The fastest learning loop is not necessarily the most intelligent one.

requirements.section: 38. From Batch Learning to Adaptive Learning
requirements.requirement_text: Update velocity should be proportional to validation maturity.

requirements.section: 39. Multimodal Context as a Future Extension
requirements.requirement_text: Moodify should keep audio evidence separable from external context so that the system can state whether a conclusion came from hearing or from metadata.
A generalized Ear may eventually test whether principles learned from AI music transfer to speech, film sound, environmental audio or industrial acoustic signals.
The AudioSet ontology and broad audio representation research demonstrate that machine listening can span many sound-event domains [27-29].
The architecture should preserve graceful degradation: a heavy model being unavailable should not erase all hearing.

The deployment architecture can scale without changing the semantic architecture. | Generation | Likely deployment change | | --- | --- | | v1 | single/few workers, CPU-first, optional learned models | | v2 | more MSE caching and structural artifacts | | v3 | vector retrieval + selected GPU inference | | v4 | larger relational/case graph services | | v5 | multi-domain model routing / scalable inference | The Production Case remains the unit of truth whether the runtime is a local CLI, one cloud worker or a distributed inference fleet.

As the Ear deepens, research roles can become more specialized without fragmenting the technical theory. | Research lens | Persistent question | | --- | --- | | WSE | what physically happened in the sound? | | MSE | what is the musical/structural organization? | | PPE | can the hearing event be trusted/reproduced? | | representation/model research | what internal state best supports hearing? | | benchmark/review | where is the capability boundary? | WSE, MSE and PPE remain useful as research disciplines even when more model specialists join.
The case-learning interface connects the disciplines: a production failure can become a WSE question, MSE question, PPE question or representation/model question.
Internal component versions can advance continuously, but a new Ear generation should require a new capability contract and benchmark.

Several patterns would weaken the long-term Ear. | Anti-pattern | Why it is dangerous | | --- | --- | | bigger model = new Ear | size does not define hearing capability | | new UI = new version | presentation is not intelligence | | remove old benchmarks | erases evidence of forgetting | | force unknown into known class | closes ontology prematurely | | rewrite historical cases | destroys scientific lineage | | use metadata shortcuts | system appears to hear without acoustic evidence | | expand scope before exit gate | dilutes falsifiable claim | | hide uncertainty to look confident | semantic authority exceeds evidence | The common theme is loss of causal understanding.
Each cell records status such as research, experimental, validated, production or deprecated.
Capability status should always link to benchmark and Production Case evidence.
For v1, that question is whether bounded physical hearing can be made reproducible.
For v2, whether context measurably improves meaning.
For v3, whether recurring AI artifacts can be recognized without shortcuts.

Each Ear generation should have a distinct exit gate. | Generation | Exit gate | | --- | --- | | v1 Basic | closed reproducible physical-hearing loop + validated bounded judgments | | v2 Contextual | context measurably improves judgment while v1 core is preserved | | v3 Artifact | validated recurring AI-artifact families + open-world restraint | | v4 Structural | structural relations support new reliable judgments | | v5 Generalized | core machinery transfers across substantially broader tasks/domains | The gates should be measured using protected benchmark suites and regression cases inherited from previous generations.
Version numbers should be earned by evidence.
The project asks whether machines can develop increasingly rich, evidence-backed and learnable representations of sound that support context-sensitive judgment.
The roadmap therefore remains a scientific sequence: Basic Hearing, Contextual Hearing, Artifact Intelligence, Structural Hearing and Generalized Auditory Intelligence.
The value of the sequence is that every step can fail independently and still teach the next research decision.
Validated previous capabilities form a protected inheritance set.** **4.
Artifact ontology grows from repeated evidence.** **6.
Learned representations add senses; they do not erase physical evidence.** **7.
Generalization must be measured across explicit axes.** **9.
Uncertainty, evidence and benchmarks must evolve with semantic authority.** **10.
Ear v5 tests whether these principles can become Generalized Auditory Intelligence.
Every later Ear inherits the physical evidence, Production Cases, errors, benchmarks and knowledge boundaries of the earlier ones.

The final chapter asks what has actually been established, what remains open, and why the most important conclusion is not that machine hearing has been solved, but that it can now be made experimentally testable.
If any link is missing, the system may still analyze audio, but the claim of auditory intelligence becomes weaker.
The earliest temptation in machine listening is to equate more measurement with more understanding.
A sufficiently large analyzer can compute thousands of descriptors, spectra, peaks, embeddings and curves.
But measurement does not tell the machine what matters.
It does not define a reference, distinguish artistic choice from technical risk, identify uncertainty or explain why one observation should become a judgment.
Moodify Ear begins when measurement is subordinated to a chain of interpretation and evidence.

requirements.section: 4. The Machine Needs an Internal Language
requirements.requirement_text: A stable representation lets physical evidence, musical structure, uncertainty and provenance coexist in one contract.

Their value comes from being localizable, reproducible and connected to explicit evidence.
The same spectral or dynamic event may be ordinary at a section boundary and unusual inside a repeated phrase.
The future of machine hearing depends on increasingly strong representations of temporal and relational organization without pretending that one symbolic theory captures all music.

requirements.section: 8. Judgment Is Where the Ear Takes Responsibility
requirements.requirement_text: A measurement can be wrong, but a judgment can also be unjustified.

requirements.section: 8. Judgment Is Where the Ear Takes Responsibility
requirements.requirement_text: That is why each judgment family requires a reference basis, evidence contract, confidence policy and abstention rule.

requirements.section: 8. Judgment Is Where the Ear Takes Responsibility
requirements.requirement_text: Eight narrow judgments that can survive review are a stronger foundation than hundreds of labels that cannot explain themselves.

One of the deepest conclusions of this book is that machine hearing must include a representation of not knowing. | State | Meaning | | --- | --- | | SUPPORTED | evidence complete and confidence meets family policy | | UNCERTAIN | evidence exists but conclusion remains weak/ambiguous | | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | required premise/evidence is missing | | UNKNOWN | unusual evidence outside known ontology | | FAILED | execution or required subsystem failed | A system that always answers may look more intelligent while being less trustworthy.
The ability to distinguish uncertainty from missing evidence, unknown phenomena and runtime failure is itself a form of intelligence.
Confidence becomes meaningful only when calibrated against real outcomes, and abstention becomes valuable only when evaluated together with coverage.

requirements.section: 10. Evidence Changes the Nature of the Claim
requirements.requirement_text: Evidence localization, provenance, counterfactual tests and explanation faithfulness make the Ear inspectable.

requirements.section: 10. Evidence Changes the Nature of the Claim
requirements.requirement_text: It is to make disagreement possible at the correct level: measurement, context, inference or conclusion.

requirements.section: 11. The Report Is Not the Intelligence
requirements.requirement_text: The Auditory Report is the human surface of the Ear, but it is not a second reasoning system.

requirements.section: 11. The Report Is Not the Intelligence
requirements.requirement_text: This protects the system from the common failure in which interface copy quietly becomes more certain than the underlying model.

requirements.section: 12. The Production Case Turns Hearing into Memory
requirements.requirement_text: This creates a technical biography for the Ear: what it heard, what it believed, how certain it was, what humans corrected and what later versions learned.

requirements.section: 13. A Learning Ear Must Remember Its Errors
requirements.requirement_text: False positives, false negatives, overconfidence, unknowns and evidence failures are part of the knowledge corpus.

requirements.section: 13. A Learning Ear Must Remember Its Errors
requirements.requirement_text: A new Ear version should be tested against its own important historical mistakes.
Candidates are validated against Golden Cases, benchmarks and protected slices.
Moodify should be able to explain not only why it made a judgment, but why its future behavior changed.

requirements.section: 15. The Intervention Lab Makes Hearing Falsifiable
requirements.requirement_text: By deliberately changing phase, bandwidth, dynamics, transients, noise or stereo relationships, Moodify can test whether the Ear responds at the right place, at the right strength and with the right uncertainty.

requirements.section: 15. The Intervention Lab Makes Hearing Falsifiable
requirements.requirement_text: The Lab is important precisely because it can show failure.

A benchmark is useful when it makes the Ear's boundary visible. | Dimension | Why it matters | | --- | --- | | precision / recall | detection correctness | | hard-negative performance | semantic restraint | | calibration | confidence reliability | | risk-coverage | quality of abstention | | localization | where the Ear heard the phenomenon | | evidence completeness | whether claims can be reconstructed | | reproducibility | whether hearing survives replay | | OOD / unknown | behavior outside validated knowledge | The result is not one flattering scalar.
It is a capability map across judgment families, domains and uncertainty conditions.
Benchmark failure is productive because it tells the research program which capability has not yet been earned.
A version number should correspond to a capability state supported by evidence.

requirements.section: 17. The First Ear Is Intentionally Small
requirements.requirement_text: Its scientific value comes from narrow closure. | Ear v1 includes | Ear v1 excludes | | --- | --- | | bounded physical judgment families | universal music-quality scoring | | minimal musical context | full universal symbolic understanding | | uncertainty / abstention | forced answer on every case | | evidence-backed Auditory Report | opaque score-only output | | Production Cases | transient untraceable runs | | offline gated learning | silent online self-modification | | Intervention benchmark | automatic mastering as canonical hearing | The objective is to prove that a bounded machine-hearing loop can be made reproducible, evidence-backed and learnable.

requirements.section: 19. The Ear Must Preserve Its Inheritance
requirements.requirement_text: This inheritance includes Golden Cases, benchmark slices, evidence contracts, representation compatibility and known historical mistakes.

requirements.section: 20. The Boundary of Knowledge Must Remain Visible
requirements.requirement_text: Chapter XIX established that some questions cannot be answered from sound alone. | Moodify does not infer from audio alone | Why | | --- | --- | | creator intention | intention is external mental/contextual information | | legal ownership/infringement | depends on law/contracts/history | | universal aesthetic quality | depends on goals, culture and preference | | medical or psychological diagnosis | different evidence/regulatory domain | | commercial success | external social/market variables | | exact causal production chain | inverse mapping is generally non-unique | These are not embarrassing exceptions.

requirements.section: 20. The Boundary of Knowledge Must Remain Visible
requirements.requirement_text: They are evidence that the system distinguishes signal information from external facts.

requirements.section: 20. The Boundary of Knowledge Must Remain Visible
requirements.requirement_text: The boundary should remain machine-readable through knowledge-limit records and visible in reports.

requirements.section: 21. Machine Hearing Does Not Need to Imitate Human Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: Moodify uses the metaphor of an Ear, but its purpose is not to reproduce the human auditory system neuron by neuron.

requirements.section: 21. Machine Hearing Does Not Need to Imitate Human Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: Human hearing depends on physiology, embodiment, memory, language, attention and culture.

requirements.section: 21. Machine Hearing Does Not Need to Imitate Human Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: Machine hearing can develop different strengths: reproducibility, exhaustive measurement, large-scale case comparison and durable evidence.

requirements.section: 21. Machine Hearing Does Not Need to Imitate Human Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: A machine-native Ear can therefore be genuinely useful while remaining unlike a human listener.

requirements.section: 21. Machine Hearing Does Not Need to Imitate Human Hearing
requirements.requirement_text: The relevant question is not whether Moodify can pass as human.

requirements.section: 22. Intelligence as Controlled Compression of Experience
requirements.requirement_text: Bad compression discards uncertainty or hides provenance.

requirements.section: 22. Intelligence as Controlled Compression of Experience
requirements.requirement_text: Good compression retains enough evidence to reconstruct why the system believed what it believed.

The Ear learns the boundary between clipping and non-clipping, between unusual and expected structure, between known and unknown artifact patterns, between supported judgment and abstention, and between what sound can establish and what requires external context.
It is a combination of representation, reference, evidence and policy.
The strongest definition developed across the book can be summarized as evidence-bearing judgment.
It is an engineering definition that can be tested.

requirements.section: 26. The Ear as a Research Instrument
requirements.requirement_text: Repeated Production Cases can reveal recurring spectral, dynamic, stereo, transient and structural phenomena that are difficult to study through isolated listening.

requirements.section: 26. The Ear as a Research Instrument
requirements.requirement_text: The benchmark can measure changing generator populations.

requirements.section: 27. The Ear as an Institutional Memory
requirements.requirement_text: The Production Case and LearningRecord architecture moves that knowledge into durable artifacts.

requirements.section: 27. The Ear as an Institutional Memory
requirements.requirement_text: The case corpus preserves the history of evidence even when the implementation around it evolves.

requirements.section: 28. The Ear as an Asset System
requirements.requirement_text: Technical assets become more valuable when they are identifiable, reproducible and connected to provenance. | Technical asset | Compounding value | | --- | --- | | Auditory Representation schemas | stable language across cases | | Judgment-family contracts | versioned semantic knowledge | | Validated Production Cases | training/retrieval/research memory | | Golden Cases | protected regression memory | | Intervention cases | causal physical ground truth | | Error Memory | historical failure patterns | | Benchmarks | measured capability boundary | | Evidence methods | reconstructable trust | | LearningRecords | traceable evolution | This turns the Ear into more than application code.

requirements.section: 28. The Ear as an Asset System
requirements.requirement_text: The organization can identify what it owns as knowledge: schemas, benchmarks, cases, reviewed phenomena, calibration records, evidence methods and release histories.
Reliable hearing requires many layers of evidence and validation.
A narrow Ear can accumulate a corpus, ontology and research method that generic assistants may not reproduce simply by adding an audio input.

requirements.section: 30. Why Physical Evidence Still Matters in the Age of Foundation Models
requirements.requirement_text: They should become part of Moodify when benchmarks justify them.

requirements.section: 30. Why Physical Evidence Still Matters in the Age of Foundation Models
requirements.requirement_text: But an embedding that performs well does not eliminate the need for direct physical evidence, especially in technical judgments.

requirements.section: 30. Why Physical Evidence Still Matters in the Age of Foundation Models
requirements.requirement_text: The future Ear should be plural: deterministic measurements, learned representations, structural models, case retrieval and human review can coexist.

requirements.section: 31. Foundation Models Change the Scale, Not the Epistemology
requirements.requirement_text: A larger model can increase capability, but it does not automatically solve calibration, causal ambiguity, evidence, OOD behavior or historical reproducibility.

requirements.section: 31. Foundation Models Change the Scale, Not the Epistemology
requirements.requirement_text: They do not eliminate the need to know what the perception means, how certain it is, which evidence supports it and how the system should learn from errors.
New generators will appear, old artifact signatures will disappear and new production workflows will emerge.
Repeated choruses, recurring phrases, stable source roles and structural patterns allow the Ear to compare like with like.
It also creates a path toward more culturally flexible machine listening because the system can learn relationships inside a piece before imposing broad population assumptions.

requirements.section: 34. The Importance of Case-Based External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: The case library provides a second kind of reference: historical validated experience.

requirements.section: 34. The Importance of Case-Based External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: A new case can be compared with reviewed predecessors without immediately changing model parameters.

requirements.section: 34. The Importance of Case-Based External Memory
requirements.requirement_text: Case retrieval also makes explanations more concrete: “this pattern resembles these reviewed cases” can be inspected rather than accepted as an abstract model score.
It is implemented through status vocabularies, uncertainty records, OOD signals, knowledge limits, abstention and non-claims.
These mechanisms protect the system from extending acoustic evidence into unsupported statements about intent, legality, health, ethics or universal quality.
A technical claim becomes meaningful when there is a clear way for it to fail.
Moodify Ear can fail an Intervention benchmark, a hard-negative test, a Golden Case replay, a calibration gate or a report-evidence audit.
These failure modes make the system scientifically legible.
A vague claim such as “Moodify understands music” is difficult to test.
A claim such as “Ear v1 detects persistent high-frequency cutoff under defined conditions with specified precision, localization and evidence completeness” can be challenged.

requirements.section: 38. The Ear and the Changing AI-Music Landscape
requirements.requirement_text: This means that Moodify's moat cannot be one fixed artifact detector.

requirements.section: 38. The Ear and the Changing AI-Music Landscape
requirements.requirement_text: The deeper asset is the methodology for discovering, validating, representing and learning new auditory phenomena.

requirements.section: 38. The Ear and the Changing AI-Music Landscape
requirements.requirement_text: An Ear that can learn the next artifact is more valuable than an Ear optimized only for the last artifact.
The long-term Moodify system should not be framed as a contest between machine hearing and human engineers.
Humans excel at intention, aesthetic context, cultural interpretation and holistic creative judgment.
Machines excel at consistency, exhaustive measurement, memory, large-scale comparison and reproducible search.
The machine can surface evidence and cases; the human can validate meaning and decide what matters.
Human authority becomes more valuable when the machine makes the evidence easier to inspect.
The Ear can reveal what happened in the audio, where it happened, how it compares with the work's own structure and what technical consequences may follow.

For a platform, the same architecture can eventually provide consistent catalog-level hearing: evidence-backed technical findings, anomaly search, provenance-aware reports and large-scale case comparison.
Because judgments and reports are versioned, Moodify can support these different operating policies without changing the underlying evidence.
Unknown clusters, intervention sensitivity curves, generator slices, structural references and human reviews can support questions that are difficult to study through public benchmarks alone.
The research value depends on careful rights governance and reproducibility.
The strongest research artifact is the validated case, not the marketing claim.
If machine-generated audio becomes a major part of the music ecosystem, new evaluation conventions may emerge around artifact quality, provenance, consistency or delivery.
It can contribute measurement methods, evidence formats and benchmark results that make future standards more concrete.
Standards become credible when multiple institutions can reproduce the underlying observations.
If it cannot, the benchmark and case system will reveal where the architecture needs to change.
If evidence cannot be made faithful for a learned family, the family may remain research-only.
The architecture should make failure informative.

Once Ear v1 exists, the next questions become sharper. | Next question | Likely Ear generation | | --- | --- | | Can context systematically improve meaning? | v2 Contextual Hearing | | Can recurring AI artifacts form validated ontology? | v3 AI Artifact Intelligence | | Can unknown artifacts be discovered before they are named? | v3 open-world hearing | | Can structure itself support new judgments? | v4 Structural Hearing | | Can source roles and symbolic views improve hearing without becoming ground truth? | v4 | | Can the same auditory machinery transfer to broader tasks/domains? | v5 Generalized Auditory Intelligence | These questions correspond directly to the v2-v5 roadmap.
The program advances when one of them can be turned into a benchmark, a case schema and an exit gate.

The Moodify research program can be summarized as four recurring activities. | Activity | Function | | --- | --- | | Observe | measure and represent what happens in sound | | Falsify | interventions, hard negatives and benchmark challenges | | Review | turn human correction into structured case knowledge | | Promote | release only validated improvements into the next Ear | Observe extends the sensors and representations.
Falsify tests known hypotheses through interventions and hard negatives.
Review turns machine error into structured human knowledge.
Promote converts only validated improvements into the next Ear.
The greatest long-term risk is not that one model is inaccurate.
Moodify should therefore treat evidence, case identity, benchmark lineage and release notes as first-class engineering outputs.
The primary output should remain an Auditory Report connected to evidence and case identity.
Additional features can grow around this core only when they preserve the distinction between listening, intervention, recommendation and external business logic.
A validated case contains much more structure than a file: measurements, representation, context, judgment, uncertainty, evidence, review and learning history.
This is the data that can support new benchmarks, retrieval systems and future models.
A sensor or encoder should enter production because it improves a defined capability under benchmark and evidence constraints.
The system should be able to compare candidate models without changing the semantic identity of the case or report.
Every important claim should eventually have a benchmark slice that can challenge it.
If Moodify says it hears clipping, there should be positive controls, hard negatives and localization tests.
If it says it detects unknown artifact patterns, there should be OOD and open-set cases.
The benchmark is therefore the operational form of intellectual honesty.
A claim without a failure test is not yet a mature capability.
This keeps human review valuable and controlled.
It also means that even a small number of carefully reviewed cases can produce compounding knowledge.
It is the first implementation of a discipline: how to convert sound into evidence-bearing machine judgment while preserving uncertainty and memory.
What should remain is the insistence that every increase in capability be made reconstructable and testable.
What remains unresolved is whether these capabilities can be integrated into a durable system that forms reliable, contextual, uncertainty-aware and revisable auditory knowledge.
It treats hearing as a closed loop of perception, representation, interpretation, judgment, evidence and learning.
It will come from whether the cases, interventions and benchmarks work.

The theory must now survive source files, noisy cases, new generators, disagreement, failed sensors, misleading correlations, calibration drift and the ordinary friction of production systems.
Moodify does not need to prove that a machine hears exactly as a human hears.
It needs to prove that a machine can build durable auditory knowledge from sound and revise that knowledge through evidence.
